comments.content:
Depends on https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/pull/13
Right now partner is able to setup bot config individually per plugin.
We should offer predefined configs so that instead of customizing each plugin individually partner could simply select a predefined config.
Simply put partner should be able to:
1. Setup each plugin individually (already implemented)
2. Create a new config from a predefined config template in one click
For the start I think we should support 2 config templates:
1. Config with all plugins from https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace and all default values
2. Minimal:
  - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop
  - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pricing
  - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards
Notice: the UI should support multiple predefined configs.

On `yarn start` getting the same errors as in [this](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/actions/runs/12077953759/job/33681602211?pr=28) CI run.
Pls fix both failing [build](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/actions/runs/12077953759/job/33681602211?pr=28) and [cypress](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/actions/runs/12077953762/job/33681602212?pr=28) workflows.

Works fine for my local org.
The main issue is how minimal and full configs are fetched:
1. Minimal is [read](https://github.com/ubq-testing/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/blob/0225e80e682eb76cf58cd85c565f222b79d03842/static/minimal-predefined.json) from json
2. Full is [loaded](https://github.com/ubq-testing/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/blob/0225e80e682eb76cf58cd85c565f222b79d03842/static/scripts/predefined-configs/template-handler.ts#L91) from another repo
I actually thought we could somehow dynamically derived a config from the plugin's [manifest.json](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/blob/111e17ddfc94eb3098f7d4de4946fd77875ef33f/manifest.json). I'll add it to a separate github issue.
